title: Авария на улице  (Crash on the Street)

segments.t: Elena accidentally hits someone with her car. She rushes out to check on the victim and realizes it is her rival, Chef Viktor. Let's listen closely to their exchange in Russian first, and then walk through each line together.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Viktor Petrovich, are you alive?' Elena turns a statement into a question purely through rising intonation on the word meaning 'living' to make the point directly in conversation.
'Huh?' Chef Viktor asks this with a single word meaning 'and', using rising intonation to turn it into a quick question.
'Oh, please forgive me.' Elena leads with the direct command form meaning 'excuse me', followed by 'oh'.
'For God's sake, forgive me.' Elena leads with the direct command form meaning 'excuse me', followed by 'God'.
'I just didn't see you.' Elena puts the word for 'just' together with 'to notice' in a crisp, natural spoken turn of phrase.
'So this is how you deal with the competition.' Chef Viktor uses the polite plural 'you' alongside 'rival', keeping a formal or respectful register.
'Here, let me help you up.' Elena leads with the direct command form meaning 'give', followed by 'lift slightly'.
'We will go to the hospital.' Elena uses the perfective verb meaning 'will be off' to focus on the single completed result, pairing it with 'the hospital'.
'It hurts.' Chef Barinov delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'it hurts'.
'We need to go to the doctor.' Here Elena anchors the line on the word meaning 'it is necessary' and builds the thought around 'to drive' and 'the doctor'.
'All right, let's go.' Chef Barinov delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'here we go'.
'Careful.' Elena delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'careful'. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.

ENG Elena accidentally hits someone with her car. She rushes out to check on the victim and realizes it. Next time you watch the episode, listen for the Russian expressions for 'living' and 'to forgive' — you will catch every word right away. See you in the next scene.

lines.fragment: Виктор Петрович, вы живы, Виктор Петрович?
Вы простите меня, ради бога, я вас просто не заметила.
